headline: Hugging Face ranks Darwin-180B-RSI #1 on five leaderboards
summary: The AI model's performance is self-reported, highlighting the importance of evaluation protocols for benchmark reproducibility.
details: Hugging Face has introduced official benchmark datasets and leaderboards, with scores derived from .eval_results/*.yaml files in model repositories. The comparability of these scores hinges on the evaluation protocol, not just the reported value.

The Darwin-180B-RSI model has achieved the top rank on five of these leaderboards. Its performance is self-reported, making the detailed protocol crucial for understanding how the scores were obtained.

The benchmarks used are all public datasets. The weights for Darwin-180B-RSI are available on Hugging Face, but serving the model requires significant hardware: a minimum of 4, and ideally 8, B200-class GPUs operating in bf16.

This initiative by Hugging Face aims to bring more transparency and reproducibility to AI model evaluations. By focusing on protocols, the platform encourages standardized reporting and allows for more reliable comparisons between different models.

headline_marked: Honor Magic 9 Pro Max [[packs 8,800mAh battery]] and Arri camera tech
headline: Honor Magic 9 Pro Max packs 8,800mAh battery and Arri camera tech
summary: The new flagship boasts a 200MP main sensor, Arri LogC3 shooting, and a massive battery, with a design inspired by vintage camera equipment.
details: Honor has launched its new Magic 9 flagship series in China, with the Pro Max model standing out due to its significant camera and battery upgrades. The design features an Arri-inspired camera island, reminiscent of the "three-lens turret" from 1937.

The collaboration with photography company Arri brings professional features to the smartphone, including Arri LogC3 shooting capabilities, 14 preset Arri Look LUTs, and support for the APV 10-bit 4:2:2 codec. The main camera uses a 200MP sensor with a 1/1.28-inch-type sensor.

Accompanying the main sensor is a 200MP 3.5x telephoto lens with a 1/1.4-inch sensor, and a 50MP ultrawide lens. The phone also includes a "cinema-grade" directional microphone for enhanced video recording and a unique square-format selfie camera.

Powering the device is a colossal 8,800mAh battery, featuring up to 40 percent silicon content for improved efficiency. The Magic 9 Pro Max is equipped with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, chosen for a complete flagship experience rather than specific benchmark pursuits.
While the Magic 9 series has debuted in China, Honor has confirmed an international launch is planned, though a specific date has not yet been announced.
